literal: Ruin will yield, without thinking if one covets; victory will yield, non-desiring which is called sublime pride.
translation: Coveting another's wealth without considering the consequences brings ruin; but the sublime pride of not desiring anything brings victory.
modern: விளைவுகளை ஆராயாமல் பிறர் பொருளை விரும்பினால் அது அழிவைத் தரும்; வேண்டாமை எனப்படும் பெருமித உணர்வு வெற்றியைக் கொடுக்கும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the destructive nature of greed with the triumphant power of contentment. If a person blindly covets another's property without thinking of the moral and practical consequences, it will lead to their utter ruin (iṟal). Conversely, cultivating the state of mind that does not desire others' possessions—described here as a sublime pride or loftiness of spirit (cerukku)—brings ultimate victory and greatness (viṟal). The word 'cerukku' usually means pride, but here it beautifully denotes the noble, self-satisfied dignity of a mind that is above greed.
